title: Resolve the Upscale Target
tests: Asks which attachment the user means, then upscales only the selected picture without guessing or processing both.

checks.name: asks first (Which of the two attached pictures should be upscaled?)

got.question: Which picture or clip should I change? Send it, or name one from earlier.

judge.summary: The lake image is visibly clearer and faithfully framed, though an increase in native pixel dimensions cannot be verified from the displayed images.

must_haves.item: The final deliverable is an upscaled version of lake-small.jpg, following clarification.
must_haves.why: The output clearly uses the selected lake photograph and improves its visible clarity and detail.

must_haves.item: The lake, mountains, trees, clouds, and their arrangement remain faithful to the selected source.
must_haves.why: The landscape features, reflections, and foreground rocks retain their original arrangement, with no conspicuous scene changes.

must_haves.item: The delivered image has larger pixel dimensions than lake-small.jpg, not merely a renamed copy.
must_haves.why: Both images are displayed at the same size, and no native file dimensions are provided. Sharper detail alone does not establish larger pixel dimensions.

must_haves.item: The full original framing and aspect ratio are preserved.
must_haves.why: The output retains the same wide aspect ratio and visible scene boundaries, including the overhanging branches and lower-right shoreline.

must_haves.item: Only one edited image is delivered; the dog photo is not included or blended into it.
must_haves.why: The single output depicts only the lake scene, with no dog imagery.
